# Codelessly layout documents: a guide for authors

This guide is for writing Codelessly user interfaces directly as JSON: screens, their layout, their look, their
data and their behavior. It describes `codelessly_api` 30.0.0, the data model the Codelessly SDK renders. Every
example on this page is checked by a test: it decodes, passes strict validation and was rendered with the SDK.

The rest of the reference is generated from the declarations in the code, so it lists every node type, prop,
field, enum value, trigger, action and formula function with its type and default:
[node types](#page-nodes), [layout](#page-layout), [decoration](#page-decoration),
[value types, models and enums](#page-values), [behaviors](#page-behaviors), [triggers](#page-triggers),
[actions](#page-actions), [bindings](#page-bindings), [formula functions](#page-formulas),
[variables, conditions and scripts](#page-variables-conditions-scripts). `catalog.json` holds the same
information as data and `document.schema.json` is a JSON Schema for a document.

<a id="guide-document"></a>
## 1. The document

A layout document is one JSON object. It holds one or more **canvases** (screens) and all their nodes in a
single flat map.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema` | Always 3 (`kSchemaVersion`). A schema-2 document (or one with none) loads, migrated in memory (`migrate2to3`). |
| `id` | The layout's id (optional). |
| `roots` | Canvas ids, in order: the screens of this page. |
| `nodes` | Every node, by id: `{"<id>": {"type": ..., ...}}`. A node's id is its key here. |
| `variables` | Variables per scope: `{"<canvas id>" \| "page_variables": [variable, ...]}`. |
| `conditions` | Conditions per canvas: `{"<canvas id>": [condition, ...]}`. |
| `scripts` | The layout's scripts (JavaScript), a list of script objects. |
| `breakpoints` | The project's breakpoints: `[{"id", "name", "minWidth", "width", "height"}]`; absent: the defaults. |

The smallest useful document: a canvas whose `body` slot holds a column with two texts.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["title", "body"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 12}
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 34}},
      "props": {"text": "Hello", "style": {"fontSize": 28, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "body": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
      "props": {
        "text": "A column with two texts, filling the screen's width.",
        "style": {"fontSize": 15, "height": 1.4, "color": "#FF4B5563"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Nothing else is needed: every key not written takes its default. A document is a **page**; a site with several
pages is either one document with several canvases in `roots`, or several documents (one file each) checked and
rendered together ([section 6](#guide-screens)).

<a id="guide-theme"></a>
### Name your palette and type scale first: the theme

A site's colors and text styles are declared once, in the site manifest's `theme` (`site.json`, next to the
pages), and named everywhere else, as a Flutter app declares a `ThemeData` and its widgets read
`Theme.of(context).colorScheme` and `.textTheme`. **Write the theme before the first page**: the palette (a name
per color the design uses) and the type scale (a name per kind of text: display, title, body, label, eyebrow...).

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "pages": ["home.json"],
  "theme": {
    "colors": {"ink": "#FF1B1B1B", "ember": "#FFE4572E", "paper": "#FFF6F1E9"},
    "textStyles": {
      "body": {"fontSize": 16, "height": 1.5, "color": "ink"},
      "title": {"from": "body", "fontSize": 32, "fontWeight": 700, "height": 1.2},
      "eyebrow": {"from": "body", "fontSize": 12, "letterSpacing": 2, "color": "ember"}
    },
    "media": [{"minWidth": 1024, "patch": {"textStyles": {"title": {"fontSize": 56}}}}]
  }
}
```

- **Colors**: `colors` maps a name to `"#AARRGGBB"` (or to another color's name: `"accent": "ember"`). Wherever a
  color is accepted (a fill, a stroke, a text's color, a shadow, an input's border or fill...), write its name:
  `"color": "ember"`. The roles `primary`, `onPrimary`, `surface`, `onSurface`, `error`, `success`, `warning`
  (keys of the theme) are names too.
- **Text styles**: `textStyles` maps a name to a [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle). A style may start
  `from` another (`"title": {"from": "body", "fontSize": 32}`) and name colors. A text names its style in one
  field: `"style": "title"`; to change some fields of it, `"style": {"from": "title", "color": "ember"}`
  (`Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge.merge(TextStyle(color: ...))`: the fields written win). Runs
  (`runs[].style`) and every other TextStyle (a button's `textStyle`, an input's) take the same two forms.
- **By screen size**: the theme's `media` rules patch the theme as a node's rules patch a node
  (`{"minWidth": 1024, "patch": {"textStyles": {"title": {"fontSize": 56}}}}`): every text using `title` grows at
  desktop width, written once. A node's own media rule may switch its style (`"patch": {"props": {"style":
  "caption"}}`, which replaces the style as a whole) or change some fields (`{"style": {"fontSize": 20}}`, merged
  over the named style).
- **Dark mode**: `"dark": {"colors": {"ink": "#FFEEEEEE"}}` gives the colors that differ in dark mode.
- Changing a color or style in the theme changes every node that names it, and only those.
- In a binding, a name is not read: bind the value, `"${theme.colors.ember}"` or `"${theme.text.title}"`.
- Validation reports a name the theme does not have (`unknown_theme_name`, with the nearest name) and a theme of
  the wrong shape (`invalid_theme`). Without a `site.json`, put the page in a directory with one:
  `{"schema": 3, "pages": ["home.json"], "theme": {...}}`.

A page using it (a fragment of `home.json`'s `nodes`):

```json
"eyebrow": {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "OUR MENU", "style": "eyebrow"}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 18}}},
"title":   {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "Fire, smoke and season", "style": "title"}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}}},
"note":    {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "Cooked over oak.", "style": {"from": "body", "color": "ember"}}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 24}}},
"rule":    {"type": "box", "layout": {"width": 120, "height": 4}, "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "ember"}]}}
```

<a id="guide-nodes"></a>
## 2. Nodes, ids and children

`nodes` maps each node's **id** to the node. The id is the map key; do not repeat it inside the node. Ids are
any text; use short readable ones (`hero-title`), and keep them unique across all documents of a site, because
actions, conditions, diagnostics and the render command name nodes by id.

Every node has a `type` (one of the [node types](#page-nodes)). Its keys:

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `String` | The node type (a key of `nodeTypes`). Required. |
| `name` | `String` |  |
| `key` | `String` | The node's name within the tree it was inserted with, unique in that tree (`"content"`): a stable handle the tree's own actions and states name it by before it has an id, kept so an export gives the tree back with its keys. Empty for none; it doesn't affect rendering. |
| `children` | `List<String>` | Ordered child ids, for types that take children. |
| `slots` | `Map<String, String>` | Named children, slot → node id, for types with slots. |
| `layout` | `Layout` | How the node sizes itself and sits in its parent (see layout). |
| `decoration` | `Decoration` | Fills, strokes, radius, shadows, blurs, clip (see decoration). |
| `props` | `Map` | The node type's own parameters (see nodeTypes). |
| `bind` | `Map<String, String>` | Bound properties: a binding path (`visible`, `props.text`, `layout.width`, `decoration.fills.<paintId>`; see `BindPaths` and DESIGN.md §5.1) → an expression (`${user.name}`, `${= qty * 2}`). |
| `actions` | `List<Reaction>` | Reactions: `{"trigger": {...}, "actions": [...]}` (see triggers, actions). |
| `component` | `ComponentLink` | The component this node is the main node of, or the top node of an instance of (DESIGN.md §4.2). |
| `media` | `List<MediaRule>` | The node's own fields by screen size, as CSS media queries: `[{"maxWidth": 599, "patch": {"props": {"direction": "vertical"}}}]`. A rule has `minWidth` and/or `maxWidth` (px, inclusive, or a breakpoint name: from its min width / up to the next one) and/or `orientation`, and a `patch` (`props`, `layout`, `decoration`, `visible`, `opacity`) merged over the node while all its conditions hold; rules apply in order, the later winning (see the guide, Responsive design). |
| `visible` | bool | Default `true`.  |
| `opacity` | double | Default `1`.  |
| behaviors |  | Flat keys for what a node does beyond layout and paint: `motion`, `scale`, `animations`, `transitions`, `shimmer`, `inkWell`, `states`, `tooltip`, `ignorePointer`, `floating`, `hero`, `flightKey`, `flight`, `draggable`, `dropTarget`, `track`, `dismissible`, `pan`, `reorderHandle`, `reveal`, `strokePath`, `typewriter`, `particles`, `textDirection`, `flip`, `tilt`, `transformGesture`, `sticky`, `viewProgress`, `measure`, `customPaint` ([behaviors](#page-behaviors)). |

**The tree is made of ids.** A parent lists its children's ids; a child does not name its parent:

- `children` is an ordered list of ids, for the types that take children: `row`, `column`, `stack`, `listView`,
  `gridView`, `pageView`, `variance` and a few more (the "Children" column below).
- `slots` maps a slot name to one id, for types with named places: a `canvas` has `body`, `appBar`,
  `floatingActionButton` and `bottomNavigationBar` (placed as Flutter's `Scaffold` places them: the app bar across
  the top at its own height, the bottom bar across the bottom, the body between, the button 16 px from the right
  and above the bottom bar); a `listTile` has `leading`, `title`, `subtitle`, `trailing`.
- Every node except a canvas has exactly one parent. A node listed under two parents, or not listed under any,
  is an error or a warning in validation. To show the same thing twice, write two nodes with their own ids.
- `roots` lists the canvases. A canvas is never a child.

There is no `Padding`, `SizedBox`, `Expanded`, `Positioned`, `Align`, `DecoratedBox` or `Opacity` node: those
Flutter wrappers are fields of the node itself (`layout`, `decoration`, `opacity`). A "card" is one `column` with
a fill, a radius and padding, not three nested widgets.

| Type | Flutter | Children | Decoration |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`canvas`](#node-canvas) | `Scaffold` | slots: `body`, `appBar`, `floatingActionButton`, `bottomNavigationBar` | yes |
| [`stack`](#node-stack) | `Stack` | `children` | yes |

<a id="guide-layout"></a>
## 3. Layout

`layout` says how big a node is and where it sits in its parent. Full field list: [layout](#page-layout).

### Width and height

Each axis has a **mode** and a **number**:

| JSON | Mode | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `120` | fixed | Exactly 120. |
| `{"hug": 120}` | hug | The size of the content (a text's lines, a row's children plus padding). |
| `{"fill": 120}` | fill | All the room the parent gives: the free space along a row's or column's main axis (shared by `flex`), the whole cross axis of a row or column, the whole box of a stack or canvas slot. |
| `{"flexible": 120}` | flexible | Up to 120, less if a row or column runs out of room (only along a row's or column's main axis). |

The number is the **design size**: the size of a fixed node, and the size used when a mode cannot apply: a fill
inside something that scrolls on that axis, or inside a parent that measures it with no limit on that axis (a
column that hugs its height, a wrapping row's line, a grid row sized to its content). The render command reports
such a fill (`fill_fallback`, naming the parent): its size is then the number you wrote, not the room you meant. For `hug` and `fill` it does not limit the size:
`{"fill": 760}` in a 1300 wide column is 1300 wide. Write the size you expect, and use
`"constraints": {"maxWidth": 760}` to cap it.

**A node without `width` or `height` is fixed at 0 and draws nothing.** Validation warns (`zero_size`). Give every
node both, except a `canvas` (its size is the screen's) and a `spacer`.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["sizing"],
  "nodes": {
    "sizing": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 400, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["hugText", "fillBox", "bar"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 400}, "height": {"fill": 400}, "padding": 10},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 8}
    },
    "hugText": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "As wide as its text", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "color": "#FF000000"}}
    },
    "fillBox": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 380}, "height": 24},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFEF4444"}]}
    },
    "bar": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["one", "two", "fixed"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 380}, "height": 40},
      "props": {"spacing": 10}
    },
    "one": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 100}, "height": {"fill": 40}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF22C55E"}]}
    },
    "two": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 200}, "height": {"fill": 40}, "flex": 2},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF3B82F6"}]}
    },
    "fixed": {"type": "box", "layout": {"width": 60, "height": 20}, "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF9CA3AF"}]}}
  }
}
```

In this example the text hugs its content, the red box fills the column's width, and in the row the green box
and the blue box share the free space 1 : 2 (`flex`) beside a fixed grey box.

### Rows, columns and flex

`row` and `column` lay their children along their **main axis** (horizontal for a row, vertical for a column).
`flex` is Flutter's `Flex`, the widget both extend: the same props plus `direction` (`horizontal` | `vertical`),
which a media rule or a binding can change, so the same children become a column at a width. They take
these props: `mainAxisAlignment` (default `start`), `crossAxisAlignment` (default **`center`**: children are
centered across the axis unless you say `start`, `end` or `stretch`), `spacing` (gap between children, default
0), `wrap` (flow onto new lines, like `Wrap`; `runSpacing` between lines), `squeezeChildren` (default true: if
the children do not fit, they shrink toward their content size instead of overflowing).

Under a row or column a child may also set, in its own `layout`:

- `flex`: its share of the free space when its main-axis size is `fill` or `flexible` (default 1);
- `align`: its alignment within its slot, as `[x, y]` from -1 to 1 or a name (`"centerRight"`); the node's box
  then spans the slot and its content sits at that alignment;
- `squeezable`: a hugging child that may shrink below its content when room runs out;
- `order` (CSS `order`): children are laid out and painted by ascending order, equal orders as listed;
- `basis` (CSS `flex-basis`, in a **wrapping** row, column or flex): the main size the child counts when lines are
  broken; a child that also fills the main axis (`{"fill": n}`) then grows by its `flex` share of what its line
  leaves. `"width": {"fill": 300}, "basis": 280` is CSS `flex: 1 1 280px`: three across at 1000 px, two at 700, one
  at 390 ([section 7](#guide-responsive)). Without `basis`, children of a wrapping row keep their own size. In a
wrapping row `crossAxisAlignment: stretch` makes the children of each line as tall as its tallest (CSS
`align-items: stretch`: equal-height cards per line).

A child hidden by a binding, a condition or a media rule takes no room and no slot: `spaceBetween` spreads the
children that show (CSS `display: none`; in Flutter, leaving it out of the list). A node written with
`"visible": false` and nothing that shows it keeps its room empty.

A `spacer` is Flutter's `Spacer`: in a row or column it takes the free space (`flex` shares it) unless it is given
a fixed size along the main axis; in a row whose width hugs its children there is no free space to take.

### Padding, margin, constraints, aspect ratio

- `padding` is space inside the node's box, around its content and children; `margin` is space outside it. A
  `text` has no padding (its box is its lines; validation warns): use `margin`, or a row with the padding around it. A negative margin does not overlap neighbours (Flutter has none):
  see **Overlapping a neighbour** below.
  Both are a number (all sides) or a list of **four** numbers `[left, top, right, bottom]`. A list of two is not
  read (it becomes 0 on every side; validation reports it).
- `constraints`: `{"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"}`, each optional. A `fill` width with
  `"maxWidth": 1100` gives a content column that grows with the window up to 1100; its parent's
  `crossAxisAlignment` (center by default) places it. Under `crossAxisAlignment: stretch` a cap holds too, as CSS
  `max-width` does over `align-items: stretch`: the child sits at the start, or where its `layout.align` puts it
  (`[0, 0]` centers it). Across a row or column, a child's width comes out as:

  | Parent's `crossAxisAlignment` | child `fill` | child `hug` | child fixed `n` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `start`, `center`, `end` | the parent's inner width, at most its `maxWidth`, placed by the alignment | its content, at most `maxWidth` | `n`, clamped by its constraints |
  | `stretch` | the parent's inner width, at most its `maxWidth` (then at the start, or at its `align`) | its content, at the start | the parent's inner width (Flutter's stretch), at most its `maxWidth` |
- `aspectRatio`: width / height the node keeps (`1.5`).
- `rotation`: degrees, clockwise, about the center; layout is unchanged.

**Overlapping a neighbour** (CSS `margin-top: -36px`, `transform: translateY(-36px)`). Flutter's answer is
`Transform.translate`: `"motion": {"translateY": -36}` moves what the node paints, not its layout, so the node
after it does not move up and the gap is kept below; a node later in its parent paints over the ones before it.
A media rule may patch it (`{"minWidth": 600, "patch": {"motion": {"translateY": -36}}}`). A card overlapping
the bottom of a hero band: the card after the hero, with `translateY: -36`, and 36 px of `margin` below it if the
next section should keep its distance. To overlap by an amount that depends on the content, use a `stack`
(children are placed by `x`/`y`, may have a negative offset in a stack with a fixed or fill size, and later ones
paint on top).

**Bleeding past the gutter** (a table or photo running to the screen's edge while the text keeps its padding):
put the padding on the children, not on the band, or let the one child that bleeds translate out of it
(`"motion": {"translateX": 18}` with a width 18 larger), and give the band `"decoration": {"clip": "none"}`
(the default). A photo frame that overhangs its photo: a `stack` with a fixed or fill size holding the frame at a
negative `x`/`y`.

### Stacks: placing children freely

A `stack` places each child by its `layout.x` and `layout.y`, measured inside the stack's padding to the child's
margin box. Each axis takes one of:

| JSON | Placement |
|---|---|
| `{"start": 16}` (or just `16`) | 16 from the left (x) or top (y) |
| `{"end": 16}` | 16 from the right or bottom |
| `{"start": 16, "end": 16}` | Stretched between: 16 from both edges. Works for fixed and fill sizes; a `hug` size keeps its own size and sits at the start. |
| `{"align": 0}` | Aligned like `Align`: -1 start, 0 center, 1 end |
| `{"relative": 300}` | 300 from the start at the stack's design size, keeping its share of the free space as the stack resizes |

`x`, `y` mean nothing under a row or column, and `flex`, `align` nothing under a stack: validation warns
(`layout_field_ignored`). Children paint in order: later ones on top. A child may sit partly outside a stack with
a fixed or fill size (a negative `start`, as Flutter's `Positioned(top: -40)`); it is clipped only if the stack's
`decoration.clip` says so. A stack that hugs its children grows to hold them, so there a negative offset is 0
(`layout_clamped`).

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["board"],
  "nodes": {
    "board": {"type": "canvas", "slots": {"body": "stage"}, "layout": {"width": 400, "height": 300}},
    "stage": {
      "type": "stack",
      "children": ["photo", "badge", "caption"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 400}, "height": {"fill": 300}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFE5E7EB"}]}
    },
    "photo": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 200, "height": 120, "x": {"align": 0}, "y": {"align": 0}},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [
          {
            "type": "linear",
            "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FF6366F1"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#FFEC4899"}]
          }
        ],
        "radius": 16
      }
    },
    "badge": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 48, "height": 48, "x": {"end": 16}, "y": {"start": 16}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF59E0B"}], "shape": "circle"}
    },
    "caption": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}, "x": {"start": 16, "end": 16}, "y": {"end": 16}},
      "props": {
        "text": "Pinned 16 px from the left, right and bottom",
        "textAlign": "center",
        "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF374151"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Which modes each parent allows (from the parents' own rules; "fill (with `basis`)": a child of a wrapping row
may fill its line's share when it sets `layout.basis`):

| Parent | Width may be | Height may be |
|---|---|---|
| `row` | fixed, fill, flexible, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, flexible, hug |
| `row` with {"wrap":true} | fixed, fill (with `basis`), hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` with {"scrollable":true} | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, hug |
| `row` with {"scrollable":true,"scrollDirection":"horizontal"} | fixed, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `stack` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `canvas` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `listView` | fill | fixed, hug |
| `listView` with {"itemExtent":80} | fill | fill |
| `gridView` | fill | fill |
| `pageView` | fill | fill |

<a id="guide-decoration"></a>
## 4. Decoration

`decoration` paints the node's box (types with "box decoration" above). Full list: [decoration](#page-decoration).

- `fills`: a list of paints, bottom to top. `{"color": "#FF2563EB"}` is a solid color. A gradient is
  `{"type": "linear" | "radial" | "sweep" | "diamond", "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": ...}, {"position": 1, "color": ...}]}`.
  As Flutter's `LinearGradient`, a linear one runs from `"begin"` to `"end"` (alignments; default left to right;
  `[0, -1]` to `[0, 1]` is top to bottom), with `"tileMode": "repeated"` repeating it past them (thin stripes:
  `"begin": [-1, 0], "end": [-0.96, 0]`). As `RadialGradient`, a radial one has a `"center"` (alignment, default
  the middle) and a `"radius"` (a share of the box's shortest side; default half its width); past the last stop
  it keeps that stop's color, so end a glow on a transparent stop. `transform` is the general form
  ([Paint](#type-Paint)). An image is `{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "...", "fit": "cover"}}`.
  A paint without `type` is an image if it has `image`, a linear gradient if it has `stops`, else a solid color.
  **A pattern in pixels** (CSS `repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, #E5E7EB 0 1px, transparent 1px 80px)`): a
  linear gradient with `"length": 80` (px from `begin` toward `end`) and `"tileMode": "repeated"`; a background grid
  is two of them, one `topCenter` → `bottomCenter`, one `centerLeft` → `centerRight` ([Paint](values.md#type-Paint)).
  **Grain**: `{"type": "noise", "noise": {"baseFrequency": 0.8, "numOctaves": 3, "seed": 1}, "color": "#FF000000",
  "opacity": 0.08}`, SVG's `feTurbulence` as a paint (a seamless tile repeated over the box; `blendMode` as CSS
  `mix-blend-mode`).
- `strokes`: paints for the border, with `strokeWidth` (default 1), `strokeAlign` (`inside`, `center`,
  `outside`), `strokeSides` (`all`, `bottom`, `topBottom`..., `none`) and `dashPattern` (`[6, 4]`). `strokeWidth` without
  `strokes` draws nothing.
- `radius`: corner radius: a number, `[x, y]`, or `[topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft]`.
- `shape`: `"circle"` paints a circle the box's shortest side across.
- `effects`: shadows and blurs, each `{"type": "dropShadow" | "innerShadow" | "layerBlur" | "backgroundBlur", ...}`
  with `color`, `offset` (`[dx, dy]`), `blurRadius`, `spreadRadius`. **An effect needs its `type`**; without it the
  effect is dropped.
- `clip`: `"antiAlias"` (or `hardEdge`) clips the content to the rounded box.
- `foregroundFills`: paints over the node **and its children**, as Flutter's `foregroundDecoration`: a scrim over a
  photo darkens a caption inside it too. For a caption over a photo, paint the photo in `fills` and put the
  darkening gradient on a child `box` before the caption (a stack: photo box, gradient box, caption text), or on
  the photo box's `foregroundFills` when the caption is a sibling painted after it.

Colors are `"#AARRGGBB"` (alpha first: `#FF` opaque, `#80` half, `#00` invisible), `"#RRGGBB"` (opaque), or the
name of a theme color (`"ember"`, [the theme](#guide-theme)). `"#FFF"`, `"rgb(...)"` and CSS names are not read.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["deco"],
  "nodes": {
    "deco": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "row"},
      "layout": {"width": 520, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF9FAFB"}]}
    },
    "row": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["card", "gradient", "outlined"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 520}, "height": {"fill": 200}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 24, "mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "card": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}],
        "radius": 12,
        "effects": [{"type": "dropShadow", "color": "#33000000", "offset": [0, 4], "blurRadius": 16}]
      }
    },
    "gradient": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [
          {
            "type": "radial",
            "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FFFDE68A"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#FFF97316"}]
          }
        ],
        "radius": [24, 4, 24, 4]
      }
    },
    "outlined": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "strokeWidth": 2, "dashPattern": [6, 4], "radius": 12}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-text"></a>
## 5. Text

A `text` node has `props.text` and `props.style`: the name of a theme text style (`"style": "body"`,
[the theme](#guide-theme)), or a [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle) (starting `from` a named one or not):
`fontSize`, `fontWeight` (100–900), `fontFamily`, `color`, `height` (line height as a multiple of the font size),
`letterSpacing`, `decoration` (`underline`...), `fontStyle` (`italic`). Also `textAlign`, `maxLines` and
`overflow` (`ellipsis`).

What a text looks like when the style leaves something out:

- **No `color`: the text is painted white.** On a light background it is invisible. Always set `color`.
- No `fontSize`: 12. No `height`: 1.33 × the font size per line. No `fontWeight`: 400. No `letterSpacing`: 0.
- No `fontFamily`: the platform's default font (Roboto on Android and the web).

Sizing: a single line `{"hug": n}` × `{"hug": n}`; a paragraph `{"fill": n}` wide (it wraps) × `{"hug": n}` high.
A fixed height shorter than the lines clips them (the render command reports `text_clipped`).

Characters the font has no glyph for (✦, ✳ in Roboto) are drawn as empty boxes; the render command reports
them (`missing_glyph`). Draw a small mark with an `icon` or a `box` with a `path` instead.

`runs` style parts of the text: `[{"start": 0, "end": 5, "style": {"fontWeight": 700}}]` (character offsets, end
exclusive, `\n` counting as one), merged over `style`; a run may carry a `"link"` URL. `text` may contain
expressions: `"Hello, ${user.name}"` ([section 8](#guide-variables)). A literal `$` right before an expression
is text: `"$${price}"` shows `$47`. There is no escape for a literal `${`: compute it (`${= '$' + '{'}`).

A raised or lowered character (a price's "$", a footnote mark): a run with `"fontFeatures": ["sups"]` (or
`"subs"`) when the font has those OpenType features (Flutter's `FontFeature.superscripts()`); otherwise a smaller
`fontSize` in the run, in a row of texts aligned `crossAxisAlignment: start` (or `baseline`) for the exact shift.

<a id="guide-screens"></a>
## 6. Screens and navigation

Each canvas in `roots` is a screen, unless canvases are grouped: canvases with the same `props.screen` are **one
screen**, one canvas per breakpoint ([section 7](#guide-responsive)). A canvas is the Flutter `Scaffold` of its
screen: put the page content in its `body` slot, usually a column filling it (`{"fill": n}` both ways). Its
`decoration.fills` is the page background. Its `layout` width and height are its design size; on a device the
canvas takes the screen's size.

Going from screen to screen is an action ([section 10](#guide-reactions)):
`{"type": "navigate", "to": "<canvas id>"}` pushes the screen; `"mode": "pop"` goes back; `"replace"` and
`"reset"` replace the history. `to` names a canvas: for a screen with a canvas per breakpoint, name any of
them; the canvas shown is the one for the current width. `"params": {"id": "${item.id}"}` passes values the
destination reads as `${route.id}`.

A site's pages may be separate documents (one file per page, checked and rendered together); `navigate` then
names a canvas id of another document. Give a canvas a `"path"` (`"pricing"`, a top-level key of the canvas
node, not a prop) for its URL; without one it gets a path from its name. The first screen of the first document
is the entry screen.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home", "about", "signup"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "slots": {"body": "homeCol"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "homeCol": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["toAbout", "openSignup", "toast"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "toAbout": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "About us"},
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "navigate", "to": "about"}]}]
    },
    "openSignup": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Sign up"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "openModal", "to": "signup", "presentation": "dialog"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "toast": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Show a toast"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "showToast", "message": "Saved", "style": "success"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "about": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "About",
      "path": "about",
      "slots": {"body": "aboutCol"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF9FAFB"}]}
    },
    "aboutCol": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["aboutTitle", "back"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "aboutTitle": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 30}},
      "props": {"text": "About", "style": {"fontSize": 24, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "back": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 120, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Back"},
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "navigate", "mode": "pop"}]}]
    },
    "signup": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Sign up",
      "slots": {"body": "signupCol"},
      "layout": {"width": 320, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "signupCol": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["signupTitle", "close"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 320}, "height": {"fill": 200}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 16}
    },
    "signupTitle": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 26}},
      "props": {"text": "Join the waitlist", "style": {"fontSize": 20, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "close": {
      "type": "filledButton",
      "layout": {"width": 120, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Close"},
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "closeModal"}]}]
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-responsive"></a>
## 7. Responsive design

Responsive layout works as on the web: flexbox and grid lay content out so it fits any width, and media queries
change what must change at a width. Use these, in this order:

1. **Intrinsic layout, no breakpoints.** A wrapping row (CSS `flex-wrap: wrap`) whose children set
   `layout.basis` (CSS `flex-basis`) and fill the main axis: lines break by the basis, and the children on each line
   grow (by `flex`, CSS `flex-grow`) to share it. Three `{"fill": n}` cards with `"basis": 280` sit three across at
   1000 px, two at 700 and one at 390; a text and a photo with `"basis": 320` sit side by side, then stack. For
   repeated data, a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent` (CSS `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))`) makes as many
   equal columns as fit. A content column capped and centered (CSS `max-width` + `margin: auto`) is a `{"fill": n}`
   width with `constraints.maxWidth`, centered by its parent's `crossAxisAlignment` (`center`, the default). A
   share of the parent (CSS `width: 60%`) is `layout.widthFactor: 0.6`.
2. **Media rules** for what must change at a width: direction, order, visibility, type size, padding. A node's
   `media` is a list of rules, each a CSS media query over the node itself:
   `{"minWidth": "tablet", "patch": {"props": {"style": {"fontSize": 40}}}}` is
   `@media (min-width: 600px) { #title { font-size: 40px } }`. `minWidth` and `maxWidth` are pixels (inclusive, as in
   CSS) or a breakpoint name (`minWidth: "tablet"`: from tablet's min width; `maxWidth: "tablet"`: up to the next
   breakpoint, so tablet and narrower); `orientation` is `portrait` or `landscape`; all conditions of a rule must
   hold. The `patch` is shaped like the node (`props`, `layout`, `decoration`, `visible`, `opacity`, `motion`, and
`bind`: below) and merged over
   it (objects merge, `null` removes a key), except that a value with several forms is **replaced**, as CSS
   replaces a declaration: `{"width": {"hug": 200}}` over `{"fill": 292}` is `{"hug": 200}` (a size, a position
   form, a paint or border of another `type`, an icon). Rules apply in order, a later one winning where two set the same field (the
   CSS cascade): write the node for phones and add `minWidth` rules for wider screens (mobile first), or the other
   way round with `maxWidth`. Validation checks every patched value as the node's own, and judges sizes at each
   range of widths with the rules that hold there (a child's `fill` against its parent as patched at the same
   widths); a finding names those widths.
   - **A row that becomes a column**: a `flex` node (Flutter `Flex`) with `"direction": "horizontal"` and a rule
     patching `"direction": "vertical"`. Its children stay the same nodes, keeping their state.
   - **Another order at a width**: each child's `layout.order` (CSS `order`; ascending, equal orders as listed),
     patched in the child's own rule: `{"maxWidth": "mobile", "patch": {"layout": {"order": -1}}}` puts it first.
   - **Hidden at a width**: `{"maxWidth": "tablet", "patch": {"visible": false}}`. A hidden node takes no room and
     no slot (CSS `display: none`).
   - Precedence: the node's own values, then its media rules, then an active interaction state's patch
     ([section 11](#guide-states)), then its bindings, then conditions. A field both patched and bound shows the
     binding (validation warns: `media_overridden`).
   - **A media rule and a binding on one field** (shown on phones only, and there only while a panel is closed):
     a patch may set `bind`, bindings that hold at its sizes only. Write the node for the other sizes and bind in
     the rule: `"visible": false, "media": [{"maxWidth": 599, "patch": {"bind": {"visible": "${= !filtersOpen}"}}}]`.
     The breakpoint stays in the media rule; the formula knows nothing of widths. To show a patched value where
     the node binds the field at other sizes, drop the binding in the rule: `"patch": {"visible": true, "bind":
     {"visible": null}}`.
   - **A full-width band with capped content** (CSS `max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto` inside a colored band):
     the band fills the width and holds the background; its one child fills with `constraints.maxWidth`, centered
     by the band's `crossAxisAlignment` (`center`, the default). Below, a comparison table built from one row
     template and one cell template ([section 13](#guide-lists)):

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 1440, "height": 900},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["band"],
      "props": {"scrollable": true},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"fill": 900}}
    },
    "band": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["rail"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"hug": 200}, "padding": [24, 48, 24, 48]},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF1F2937"}]}
    },
    "rail": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["title", "table"],
      "props": {"spacing": 16, "crossAxisAlignment": "stretch"},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 160}, "constraints": {"maxWidth": 1200}}
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "text",
      "props": {"text": "Compare plans", "style": {"fontSize": 28, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 34}}
    },
    "table": {
      "type": "listView",
      "children": ["tr"],
      "bind": {"data": "${rows}"},
      "props": {"physics": "never"},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 120}}
    },
    "tr": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["label", "cells"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1200}, "height": {"hug": 44}},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF374151"}], "strokeSides": "bottom"}
    },
    "label": {
      "type": "text",
      "bind": {"props.text": "${item.label}"},
      "props": {"text": "", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FFD1D5DB"}},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 180}, "height": {"hug": 20}, "flex": 2}
    },
    "cells": {
      "type": "gridView",
      "children": ["cell"],
      "bind": {"data": "${item.values}", "props.crossAxisCount": "${= length(item.values)}"},
      "props": {"physics": "never", "crossAxisCount": 3, "shrinkWrapRows": true},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 44}, "flex": 3}
    },
    "cell": {
      "type": "text",
      "bind": {"props.text": "${item}"},
      "props": {"text": "", "textAlign": "center", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}},
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 200}, "height": {"hug": 20}, "margin": [0, 12, 0, 12]}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "home": [
      {
        "name": "rows",
        "type": "list",
        "value": [
          {"label": "Seats", "values": ["5", "25", "Unlimited"]},
          {"label": "SSO", "values": ["–", "Yes", "Yes"]},
          {"label": "Support", "values": ["Email", "Chat", "24/7"]}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
3. **Bindings on `${screen}`** for values computed from the size, the escape hatch:
   `"bind": {"layout.width": "${= min(screen.width - 32, 760)}"}`. `${screen}` has `width`, `height`,
   `breakpoint` (the id), `is.<name>` and `atLeast.<name>` (`${= screen.atLeast.tablet ? 3 : 1}`), and
   `isMobile`/`isTablet`/`isDesktop` (one per breakpoint id). `${screen.width}` prints a decimal (`390.0`);
   `${= screen.width}` prints `390`. Nothing can check such a formula's result type: prefer media rules.
4. **A canvas per breakpoint**, only for screens that are genuinely different designs. Canvases with the same
   `props.screen` are one screen; each sets `props.breakpoint` to the breakpoint it is for. At a given width the
   screen shows the canvas whose breakpoint's `minWidth` is the highest at or below the width, else its narrowest.
   Each canvas has its own nodes; share state with `page_variables` ([section 8](#guide-variables)). A `variance`
   node does the same for one part of a screen.

The project's **breakpoints** name size classes by minimum width. Unless a document's `breakpoints` key says
otherwise they are:

| id | name | minWidth | design width × height |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile` | Mobile | 0 | 390 × 844 |
| `tablet` | Tablet | 600 | 834 × 1112 |
| `desktop` | Desktop | 1024 | 1440 × 900 |

This page uses all four web patterns: a header whose links collapse to a menu icon below desktop (media rules on
`visible`), a 3 → 2 → 1 card grid from data with no breakpoint (`minCrossAxisExtent`), a text-and-photo section
that stacks with the photo first on phones (`basis` in a wrapping row, the photo's `order` patched), and a title
whose size steps up with the width (media rules on `fontSize`), inside a content column capped at 1200 and
centered:

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 1440, "height": 900},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["header", "content"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"fill": 900}},
      "props": {"scrollable": true}
    },
    "header": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["logo", "nav", "menu"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": 64, "padding": [16, 0, 16, 0]},
      "props": {"mainAxisAlignment": "spaceBetween"},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF111827"}]},
      "media": [{"minWidth": "desktop", "patch": {"layout": {"padding": [32, 0, 32, 0]}}}]
    },
    "logo": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"text": "Relay", "style": {"fontSize": 20, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}}
    },
    "nav": {
      "type": "row",
```

The same page in CSS:

```css
#nav { display: none } @media (min-width: 1024px) { #nav { display: flex } #menu { display: none } }
#plans { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: 24px }
#split { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px 48px } #split > * { flex: 1 1 320px }
@media (max-width: 599px) { #split-photo { order: -1 } }
#title { font-size: 32px } @media (min-width: 600px) { #title { font-size: 40px } }
@media (min-width: 1024px) { #title { font-size: 56px } }
#content { max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto }
```
