<a id="guide-variables"></a>
## 8. Variables, bindings and expressions

**Variables** hold a screen's state. Declare them in the document's `variables`, under a canvas id (that canvas
only) or under `"page_variables"` (every canvas of the document, kept while the user moves between them):

```json
"variables": {"page_variables": [{"name": "annual", "type": "boolean", "value": false}]}
```

Types: `integer`, `text`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `color`, `list`, `map`, `image`, `choice`. `value` is written as the type holds it in JSON: `3`, `2.5`, `true`, `"text"`,
`"#FF2563EB"`, `[...]`, `{...}`.

**Computed variables** define a value once: a variable with a `formula` (what goes in `${= ...}`) is read-only and
follows what it reads. **Function variables** add `parameters` and are called by name from any formula. Declare
them in `page_variables` to share them with every canvas of the document (a screen's breakpoint canvases too):

```json
"variables": {"page_variables": [
  {"name": "query", "type": "text", "value": ""},
  {"name": "dishes", "type": "list", "value": [{"name": "Lamb", "vegan": false}, {"name": "Squash", "vegan": true}]},
  {"name": "shown", "type": "list", "formula": "filter(dishes, d => contains(lower(d.name), lower(query)))"},
  {"name": "count", "type": "integer", "formula": "length(shown)"},
  {"name": "usd", "type": "text", "parameters": ["n"], "formula": "'$' + round(n)"}
]}
```

`${shown}` feeds a list, `${count}` a label, `${= usd(price * 12)}` any text, wherever they are needed: write a
filter or a rule once, not in every binding. A function variable's name must not be a formula function's
([formula functions](#page-formulas)): the built-in one wins.

**Expressions** are text that reads values:

- `${name}` or `${path}` reads a value: `${count}`, `${user.name}`, `${items[0].price}`, `${item.title}`.
- `${= formula}` computes one: `${= count * price}`, `${= annual ? 'Yearly' : 'Monthly'}`,
  `${= money(total, '$')}`. Operators: `+ - * / %`, comparisons, `&&`, `||`, `!`, `a ? b : c`; functions are
  listed in [formula functions](#page-formulas).
- A text that is exactly one expression gives its value with its type (a number stays a number, a list a list);
  any other text with `${...}` is text with the values inserted.

Names an expression can start with: the screen's variables and `data`, `route`, `storage`, `screen`, `theme`, `item`, `index`, `parent`, `result`, `loop`, `auth`, `drag`, `perf`, `track`, `dismiss`, `pan`, `transform`, `flip`, `tilt`, `view`, `sticky`, `script`, `speech`, `pageOffset`. `screen` and `route` are described
above; `item` and `index` exist inside a list's item ([section 13](#guide-lists)); `result` is what the previous
action of a chain gave.

**Bindings** put an expression on a field. `bind` maps a **binding path** to an expression; the field takes the
value whenever the names it reads change:

```json
"bind": {"props.text": "${= 'Total: ' + money(count * price, '$')}", "visible": "${= count > 0}"}
```

Literals are not names: `${false}` reads a variable called `false`; write `${= false}` (or just `false` in the
field, without a binding).

Paths: `visible`, `opacity`, `layout.<field>` (`layout.width`), `decoration.fills[0].color`,
`decoration.radius`, `props.<prop>` and `props.<prop>.<field>` (`props.style.color`), `data` (a list's items),
`selected`, `disabled`, and behavior keys. Full list: [bindings](#page-bindings). Values are read loosely
(`"12"` is a number, `"#FF0000"` a color); a value that cannot be read leaves the field as it was. A text's
`props.text` may hold `${...}` directly, without `bind`. Other fields do not evaluate expressions written in them:
`"opacity": "${x}"` is an error; write `"bind": {"opacity": "${x}"}`.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["counter"],
  "nodes": {
    "counter": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["label", "total", "add"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 400}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "label": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"text": "Clicked ${count} times", "style": {"fontSize": 18, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "total": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF6B7280"}},
      "bind": {"props.text": "${= 'Total: ' + money(count * price, '$')}"}
    },
    "add": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 44},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 8},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "count", "op": "add", "value": "1"}]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "counter": [{"name": "count", "type": "integer", "value": 0}, {"name": "price", "type": "decimal", "value": 2.5}]
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-conditions"></a>
## 9. Conditions

A condition sets node fields while a test holds: an ordered list of branches (if, else if, ..., else). It lives
in the document's `conditions`, under a canvas id. Each branch has `when` (a predicate; none for the final else)
and `set`, a list of `{"node": id, "path": binding path, "value": value}`. A predicate is
`{"left": "${annual}", "op": "isTrue"}`, `{"left": "${count}", "op": "greaterThan", "right": "5"}`, or
`{"and": [...]}` / `{"or": [...]}`.

| op | Reads right | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `equalsTo` | yes |  |
| `notEqualsTo` | yes |  |
| `greaterThan` | yes |  |
| `lessThan` | yes |  |
| `greaterThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `lessThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `isEmpty` | no | Null, or an empty text, list or map. |
| `isNotEmpty` | no |  |
| `contains` | yes | A list holds the right operand, a text contains it, a map has it as a key. |
| `isOdd` | no |  |
| `isEven` | no |  |
| `isNull` | no | Null, or the text `null`. |
| `isTrue` | no |  |
| `isFalse` | no |  |

For one field the first branch that holds and sets it wins; a condition wins over the node's binding, which wins
over the node's own value. A binding with a formula is often simpler; conditions suit setting several nodes at
once.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["plans"],
  "nodes": {
    "plans": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["toggle", "price", "note"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 300}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "toggle": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["toggleLabel"],
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 36}, "padding": [14, 8, 14, 8]},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 18},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "annual", "op": "toggle"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "toggleLabel": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Monthly", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF2563EB"}},
      "bind": {"props.text": "${= annual ? 'Annual billing' : 'Monthly billing'}"}
    },
    "price": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
      "props": {"text": "$12 / month", "style": {"fontSize": 32, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "note": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Save 20% with annual billing", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF16A34A"}}
    }
  },
  "variables": {"plans": [{"name": "annual", "type": "boolean", "value": false}]},
  "conditions": {
    "plans": [
      {
        "id": "billing",
        "branches": [
          {
            "when": {"left": "${annual}", "op": "isTrue"},
            "set": [
              {"node": "price", "path": "props.text", "value": "$120 / year"},
              {"node": "note", "path": "visible", "value": false}
            ]
          },
          {"set": [{"node": "price", "path": "props.text", "value": "$12 / month"}]}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-reactions"></a>
## 10. Reactions: triggers and actions

A node's `actions` is a list of **reactions**. A reaction is a **trigger** and the chain of **actions** it runs, in
order:

```json
"actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"},
             "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "count", "op": "add", "value": "1"},
                         {"type": "navigate", "to": "thanks"}]}]
```

- Triggers ([all](#page-triggers)): `click`, `hover`, `cursorEnter`/`cursorExit`, `longPress`, `changed`
  (an input's value changed), `submitted`, `load` (on a canvas: the screen appeared), `valueChanged` (a variable
  changed), `timer`, `scroll`, `enterViewport`... A trigger may be written as just its type: `"trigger": "click"`.
- Actions ([all](#page-actions)) include `setVariable` (`op`: `set` (default), `toggle`, `add`, `subtract`,
  `insert`, `removeAt`...; `value` is an expression), `navigate`, `openModal`, `closeModal`, `showToast`,
  `openLink` (`url`), `if` (`condition`: a predicate; `then` and `else`: action lists), `delay` (`ms`),
  `scrollTo` (`node`), `setValue`, `submitForm`, `callApi`.
- In a chain `${result}` starts as the trigger's event (a text field's `changed`: its text; a checkbox's: its
  value) and is replaced only by an action that gives a value (`callApi`, `openModal`'s closing value,
  `runScript`, `callFunction`, a cloud read); `setVariable`, `navigate`, `showToast`, `scrollTo`... leave it as it
  was, so every action of a `changed` chain can read the text as `${result}`.
- A tap on a control (a checkbox, a switch, a button, a text field) inside a node with a `click` reaction runs the
  control's own reaction only, as Flutter's gesture arena gives the tap to the innermost recognizer; a tap beside
  the control runs the row's. To toggle from the whole row with one handler, give the control
  `"ignorePointer": true` and bind its value.
- Every action also takes `enabled`, `nonBlocking` and `when` (a predicate: run only while it holds).
- **Keys**: a canvas's `keyDown` reaction (`{"trigger": {"type": "keyDown", "key": "ArrowRight"}, ...}`) runs
  while no text field has the focus: arrow keys between tabs are two reactions that set the tab variable
  (`${= (tabIndex + 1) % 4}`), Escape closing a menu is one. The render command presses keys with `--key
  ArrowRight` (after `--unfocus` if a field has the focus).

Write each action's fields flat in the action object, exactly as named in [actions](#page-actions);
a misspelled key is dropped silently by the runtime and reported by validation (`unknown_action_key`).

<a id="guide-states"></a>
## 11. Hover, press and other states

`states` on a node changes it and its descendants while it is `hovered`, `pressed`, `focused`, `selected`,
`disabled` or `dragged`. Each state maps node ids (the node itself or nodes inside it) to a **patch**: partial node
JSON merged over that node (objects merge, other values replace, `null` removes).

`selected` and `disabled` follow bindings: `"bind": {"selected": "${= tab == 'pricing'}"}` puts the node in its
`selected` state. `hovered` needs a mouse: on touch screens it never happens, so do not hide anything behind it.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["buttons"],
  "nodes": {
    "buttons": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["cta"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 200}},
      "props": {"mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "cta": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["ctaLabel"],
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 160}, "height": {"hug": 44}, "padding": [20, 12, 20, 12]},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 10},
      "states": {
        "hovered": {
          "cta": {"decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF1D4ED8"}]}},
          "ctaLabel": {"props": {"text": "Let's go"}}
        },
        "pressed": {"cta": {"opacity": 0.8}}
      },
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "openLink", "url": "https://example.com"}]}]
    },
    "ctaLabel": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Get started", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-scrolling"></a>
## 12. Scrolling

A screen scrolls only if something in it scrolls. Make the canvas's body column scroll:
`"props": {"scrollable": true}` with `{"fill": n}` width and height. Its children keep their sizes and the column
scrolls when they are taller than the screen. Without it, content past the bottom of the screen is cut off on a
device (the render command reports `offscreen`). Inside a scrolling column, a child cannot `fill` the scrolling
axis (there is no end to fill to). Rows scroll sideways with `"scrollable": true, "scrollDirection": "horizontal"`.

`scrollTo` reveals a node (`"node"`: an id, or an expression giving one: `"node": "col-${step}"`; `"axis":
"horizontal"` moves only sideways scroll views). A comparison table with a **sticky first column** on phones is
two columns side by side: a fixed column of row labels, and a row of plan columns that scrolls sideways (made to
scroll only on phones by a media rule on its `scrollable`); give each table row the same height in both.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["article"],
  "nodes": {
    "article": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "scroller"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "scroller": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["header", "p1", "p2", "p3"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"scrollable": true, "spacing": 16, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "header": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFDBEAFE"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p1": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFDE68A"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p2": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFBBF7D0"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p3": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "The end of the page.", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-lists"></a>
## 13. Lists and repeated data

A `listView` (or `gridView`, `pageView`) repeats its **first child** once per item of its `data` binding:
`"bind": {"data": "${questions}"}`. Inside the repeated child, `${item}` is the item (`${item.title}`) and `${index}`
its position from 0. A list in a scrolling page sets `"scrollable": false` so it lays out every item at its full
height; `spacing` separates items. Items fill the list's width.

For cards in columns from one list, inside a scrolling page, use a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent` (CSS
`repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr))`: as many equal columns as fit), `"shrinkWrapRows": true` (each row as tall
as its tallest card, the cards stretched to it: equal heights) and `"physics": "never"` (it lays out every item and
the page scrolls), as in [section 7](#guide-responsive). A `listView` with `"wrap": true` lays its items out at
their own sizes in runs along its `scrollDirection`: with the default `vertical` they flow top to bottom into
columns (`vertical_wrap`); set `"scrollDirection": "horizontal"` for chips side by side.

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["faq"],
  "nodes": {
    "faq": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 600},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["heading", "items"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 600}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start", "scrollable": true}
    },
    "heading": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 30}},
      "props": {"text": "Questions", "style": {"fontSize": 24, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "items": {
      "type": "listView",
      "children": ["item"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 300}},
      "props": {"scrollable": false, "spacing": 8},
      "bind": {"data": "${questions}"}
    },
    "item": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["q", "a"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 60}, "padding": 12},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 4},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF3F4F6"}], "radius": 8},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "open", "value": "${= open == index ? -1 : index}"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "q": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 318}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.q}", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "a": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 318}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.a}", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "height": 1.4, "color": "#FF4B5563"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${= open == index}"}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "faq": [
      {"name": "open", "type": "integer", "value": -1},
      {
        "name": "questions",
        "type": "list",
        "value": [
          {"q": "Can I cancel any time?", "a": "Yes. Your plan stays active until the end of the period."},
          {"q": "Do you offer refunds?", "a": "Within 14 days of purchase, no questions asked."},
          {"q": "Is there a free trial?", "a": "Every plan starts with 30 days free."}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The same item template can carry reactions: a click on an item runs with that item's `item` and `index`.

**Nested lists.** A list inside a list's item repeats per item of its own `data`, usually a field of the outer
item: sections, then each section's dishes, then each dish's tags. Inside the inner template `item` and `index`
are the innermost list's; `parent` is the item around it (`${parent.item}`, `${parent.index}`, and its fields
directly: `${parent.name}`). Two levels:

```json
"sections": {"type": "listView", "children": ["section"], "bind": {"data": "${= groupBy(dishes, 'section')}"},
             "props": {"scrollable": false, "spacing": 24}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 400}}},
"section":  {"type": "column", "children": ["sectionTitle", "dishList"], "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start"},
             "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 200}}},
"sectionTitle": {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "${item.key} (${item.count})", "style": {"fontSize": 20, "color": "#FF111827"}},
             "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 24}}},
"dishList": {"type": "listView", "children": ["dish"], "bind": {"data": "${item.items}"}, "props": {"scrollable": false},
             "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 120}}},
"dish":     {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "${parent.key} ${parent.index}: ${item.name} (#${index})", "style": {"color": "#FF374151"}},
             "layout": {"width": {"fill": 600}, "height": {"hug": 20}}}
```

A third level reads the second's item as `parent`; to reach further out, carry the value down in the data.

**A table from one template**: a `listView` of rows bound to the records, each row a label and a `gridView` of
cells bound to `${item.values}` with `crossAxisCount` the number of columns: one cell node for every column (the
example in [section 7](#guide-responsive)). Four columns written by hand, or four lists side by side, are the same
table written four times; for a column that stays while the others scroll sideways, keep the label column a
`listView` of its own beside one horizontally scrolling block of the cell grids.

**Equal-height cards** in a `gridView` with `"shrinkWrapRows": true` (CSS grid's auto rows): each row is as tall as
its tallest item, and every item is stretched to it (`align-items: stretch`), whether it hugs or fills its height.
Make the item the card (the box with the decoration): a card *inside* a hugging item column keeps its own height,
as a CSS card inside a stretched grid item does, and a card that fills the item's height there takes its design
number (`fill_fallback`). A banner above one card goes inside the card (the item), with a top margin on the
others to line them up. `shrinkWrapRows` wins over `mainAxisExtent` (validation warns:
`prop_ignored`); for rows at least n tall, keep it and give the item `"constraints": {"minHeight": n}`.

<a id="guide-forms"></a>
## 14. Forms and inputs

Inputs are Material widgets: `textField`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `radio`, `slider`, `dropdown`,
`segmentedButton`, `datePicker`. Each reports its value through its `changed` trigger as `${result}`; store it in a
variable with `setVariable`. A text field's label and hint are in `props.decoration`
([InputDecoration](#type-InputDecoration): `labelText`, `hintText`, `helperText`, `filled`,
`fillColor`, `border`...).

Validate with variables: keep the values, set a `tried` flag on submit, and show error texts with `visible`
bindings (or bind `props.decoration.errorText`). The `validator` prop of a text field is declared but not applied
by the SDK, and `inputFormatter` only applies `{"type": "regex", "pattern": ..., "allow": true}`. An outlined
field (`"border": {"type": "outline", ...}`) needs `"contentPadding": [14, 16, 14, 16]` in its decoration to keep
its text off the border.

**A text field bound to a variable**: bind its `props.initialValue` to the variable (`"bind": {"props.initialValue": "${query}"}`).
That is a two-way binding, as a Flutter `TextEditingController` held in state: typing sets the variable (its
`changed` reaction also runs), and setting the variable elsewhere (a clear button, `--set`) changes the text, keeping
the caret. The render command types with `--type <id>=<text>`: the text replaces what the field held.

**A clear button in the field** ("×"): its `decoration.suffixIcon` with a tap reaction (`actions` is a list of
reactions, as a node's), shown only while there is text by binding the icon:

```json
"search": {"type": "textField", "layout": {"width": {"fill": 280}, "height": 44},
  "bind": {"props.initialValue": "${query}", "props.decoration.suffixIcon.icon": "${= query == '' ? '' : 'close'}"},
  "props": {"decoration": {"hintText": "Search dishes", "suffixIcon": {"icon": "close", "size": 18,
    "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "query", "value": ""}]}]}}}}
```

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["contact"],
  "nodes": {
    "contact": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 500},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["email", "emailError", "send", "thanks"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 500}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 8, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "email": {
      "type": "textField",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 56},
      "props": {"decoration": {"labelText": "Email", "hintText": "you@example.com"}, "keyboardType": "emailAddress"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "changed"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "email", "value": "${result}"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "emailError": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 18}},
      "props": {"text": "Enter a valid email address.", "style": {"fontSize": 13, "color": "#FFDC2626"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${= tried && !contains(email, '@')}"}
    },
    "send": {
      "type": "elevatedButton",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": 44},
      "props": {"label": "Send"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [
            {"type": "setVariable", "variable": "tried", "value": "true"},
            {
              "type": "if",
              "condition": {"left": "${= contains(email, '@')}", "op": "isTrue"},
              "then": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "sent", "value": "true"}]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "thanks": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Thanks! We'll reply within a day.", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FF16A34A"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${sent}"}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "contact": [
      {"name": "email", "type": "text", "value": ""},
      {"name": "tried", "type": "boolean", "value": false},
      {"name": "sent", "type": "boolean", "value": false}
    ]
  }
}
```

**Styling the controls, in one place:**

| Control | Its look | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `textField` | border (`"border": {"type": "outline", "borderSide": {"color": ..., "width": 1}, "borderRadius": 8}`), `focusedBorder`, `errorBorder`, `fillColor` + `filled`, `contentPadding`, `hintStyle`, `labelStyle`, `prefixIcon`/`suffixIcon` | `props.decoration` ([InputDecoration](#type-InputDecoration)) |
| `textField` | the typed text's style, the caret (`cursorColor`, `showCursor`), the focus ring (`focusRingColor`, `focusRingWidth`) | `props` ([textField](#node-textField)) |
| `checkbox` | `activeColor`, `checkColor`, `fillColor`, `side` / `activeSide` (the box's border), `borderRadius`, `compact` | `props` ([checkbox](#node-checkbox)) |
| `switch` | `activeTrackColor`, `inactiveTrackColor`, `activeThumbColor`, `inactiveThumbColor`, `fillTrack`, `thumbInset`, `trackOutlineWidth`, `trackRadius` | `props` ([switch](#node-switch)) |
| a labelled row | a `row` holding the control (with `"ignorePointer": true` and its value bound) and a text, with the row's `click` reaction | [section 10](#guide-reactions) |

Every color there may be a theme color's name.

Buttons (`elevatedButton`, `filledButton`, `outlinedButton`, `textButton`) take `label` and `style`
([ButtonStyle](#type-ButtonStyle): `backgroundColor`, `foregroundColor`, `textStyle`, `shape`...).
Their label text is 12 px unless `style.textStyle.fontSize` says otherwise. Give buttons a fixed width: a hugging
button is only as wide as its label, without padding. For full control of a button's look, use a `row` with a
decoration, padding, a text child and a `click` reaction, as in [section 11](#guide-states).

<a id="guide-modals"></a>
## 15. Modals and toasts

`{"type": "openModal", "to": "<canvas id>"}` shows another canvas over the screen, at its design size
(`presentation`: `dialog`, `bottomSheet`, `fullScreen`...). Inside it, `{"type": "closeModal"}` closes it. The modal
canvas is a root like any screen; give it the size of the dialog.
`{"type": "showToast", "message": "Saved", "style": "success"}` shows a short message.
See the navigation example in [section 6](#guide-screens).

<a id="guide-images"></a>
## 16. Images, icons and fonts

- **Images** are image fills: `{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "...", "fit": "cover"}}` in `decoration.fills`
  of a box (give the box the image's size or an `aspectRatio`). The SDK loads `https://` URLs and `data:image/...`
  URLs. For drafts, the render command also reads a path relative to the document (`"assets/photo.png"`) and
  inlines it; a real publish needs the image uploaded and its URL. The render command does not fetch network
  images: it reports them (`image_network`) and leaves them blank.
- **Icons**: an `icon` node with `props.icon` set to a Material icon name (`"check_circle"`, `"menu"`,
  `"arrow_forward"`, `"north_east"`; any name at fonts.google.com/icons; `_outlined`, `_rounded`, `_sharp` suffixes
  pick the style), `props.color` and `props.size` (Flutter's `Icon.size`: the glyph's size, centered in the node's
  box; without it the glyph fills the box; a hugging icon takes its size). The glyph is written the same way
  everywhere: a text field's `decoration.prefixIcon` is `{"icon": "search", "size": 18}`. A name the renderer does not know draws nothing
  (`icon_not_drawn`).
- **Fonts**: `style.fontFamily` names a family (`"Inter"`), with `fontWeight` choosing the file. An app fetches
  Google Fonts by name. The render command uses font files from `--fonts <dir>` (`.ttf`, `.otf`, `.woff`, read
  by their real family and weight; a font package folder such as `node_modules/@fontsource/<family>` works as it is;
  `--fonts system` adds the system's fonts; of a package's subset files for one face, the one with Latin text's
  characters is used) plus Roboto, and reports a family it does not have (`font_fallback`:
  the family, weight and style asked for and where it looked).

```json
{
  "schema": 3,
  "roots": ["gallery"],
  "nodes": {
    "gallery": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 360},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["photo", "caption"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 360}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "photo": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "assets/photo.png", "fit": "cover"}}],
        "radius": 12,
        "clip": "antiAlias"
      }
    },
    "caption": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["check", "captionText"],
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"spacing": 6}
    },
    "check": {
      "type": "icon",
      "layout": {"width": 20, "height": 20},
      "props": {"icon": "check_circle", "color": "#FF16A34A"}
    },
    "captionText": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "An image fill and a Material icon", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF374151"}}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-checking"></a>
## 17. Checking your work

Decoding is lenient: a misspelled key, a value of the wrong shape or an unknown enum value is silently ignored or
replaced by its default. Never trust a document that has not been checked.

Run the render command from the SDK repository (`tool/render/README.md` there has the details):

```sh
tool/render/render.sh site/ --out shots/ --sizes 390x844,834x1112,1440x900 --full-page
```

It validates every document strictly, renders each screen with the SDK at each size, writes
`shots/<screen>@<w>x<h>.png` and `shots/diagnostics.json`, and prints one line per problem with a code, the
JSON pointer of the value (`/nodes/hero-title/props/style/fontSize`) or the node, and what to do. It exits 1 when
there are errors. Interactions before the capture, in order: `--tap <id>` (`<id>#<n>` for the n-th copy of a list
item; a node out of view or under an overlay is scrolled to the middle first, and a tap that would land on another
node is reported, not made), `--hover <id>`, `--focus <id>`, `--type <id>=<text>`, `--set <variable>=<json>`,
`--scroll <id or screen>=<px>`, `--navigate <canvas id>`, `--wait <ms>`. A step may name a node by its `name`
too: give the matching nodes of a screen's breakpoint canvases the same `name` and one step reaches whichever is
shown. `--label <name>` keeps the screenshots and `diagnostics-<name>.json` of each state apart. `--full-page`
captures the whole page from its top (whatever a step scrolled it to), its own scroll height, with content fixed to
the window drawn in the first window; without it the capture is the window where the steps left the page. Every
diagnostic is about the page as it renders at that size: its media rules applied, what scrolls there, what an
ancestor clips away.
Look at the screenshots: validation cannot tell you that a page is ugly.

Validation codes (from `package:codelessly_api/validate.dart`):

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_document` | error | The document is not a JSON object, or a top-level key has the wrong shape (nodes not an object, roots not a list). |
| `schema_version` | warning | The document has no "schema", or one this package does not read (it reads 2 and 3, and writes 3). |
| `schema_outdated` | info | A schema-2 document: it loads, migrated to schema 3 in memory (`migrate2to3`; `dart run tool/migrate.dart` rewrites the file). The other diagnostics are of the migrated document. |
| `legacy_value` | warning | A `legacy.<name>` key the schema-3 migration kept: a value that had no schema-3 form and is no longer read. |
| `unknown_document_key` | error | A top-level key of the document that nothing reads. |
| `dangling_root` | error | A root id that names no node. |
| `root_not_canvas` | warning | A root that is not a canvas: it is never shown as a screen. |
| `no_roots` | error | The document has no roots, so nothing is shown. |
| `invalid_node` | error | A node that is not an object or has no "type": decoding drops it. |
| `unknown_node_type` | error | A node type no declaration knows: it renders as an empty box. |
| `unknown_node_key` | error | A key on a node that is neither a node field nor a behavior: it is kept but does nothing. |
| `unknown_prop` | error | A key in "props" that the node type does not declare: it does nothing. |
| `unknown_layout_key` | error | A key in "layout" that layout does not read. |
| `unknown_decoration_key` | error | A key in "decoration" that decoration does not read. |
| `unknown_field` | error | A key inside a value (a paint, a text style, a behavior model...) that its type does not read. |
| `wrong_type` | error | A value of the wrong JSON type or shape: decoding ignores it and uses the default. |
| `loose_value` | warning | A value of another JSON type that decoding converts (the text "12" for a number): write the type itself. |
| `invalid_enum` | error | A value that is not one of the allowed names: decoding uses the default. |
| `out_of_range` | error | A number outside its declared bounds: decoding clamps it. |
| `decoration_ignored` | warning | Fills, strokes, radius or shadows on a type without a box decoration: only blur effects are kept. |
| `dangling_child` | error | A child id that names no node. |
| `dangling_slot` | error | A slot whose id names no node. |
| `multiple_parents` | error | A node listed as a child (or slot) of more than one parent, or twice in one parent. |
| `cycle` | error | A node that contains itself. |
| `unreachable_node` | warning | A node no root reaches: it is never shown. |
| `unknown_slot` | error | A slot name the node type does not have. |
| `children_not_allowed` | error | A "children" list on a type that takes none (or takes slots only): they are never shown. |
| `slots_not_allowed` | error | A "slots" map on a type that has no slots. |
| `canvas_as_child` | error | A canvas used as the child of another node: canvases are screens, only roots. |
| `layout_field_ignored` | warning | A layout field the node's parent does not read (x/y outside a stack, flex/align outside a row or column). |
| `fit_not_allowed` | warning | A width or height mode the parent cannot honor (fill along a scrolling axis, flexible outside a row/column). |
| `zero_size` | warning | A fixed width or height of 0 (often a missing "width"/"height"): the node is invisible. |
| `vertical_wrap` | warning | A wrapping list that scrolls vertically: its items flow top to bottom and wrap into columns, not side by side. |
| `layout_clamped` | warning | A layout value that cannot take effect as written: a negative offset in a stack that hugs its children (clamped to 0), or a negative margin (Flutter has none: the box shrinks). |
| `prop_ignored` | warning | A prop that has no effect with another the node sets (a grid's mainAxisExtent while shrinkWrapRows sizes its rows): one of them is ignored. |
| `unknown_bind_path` | error | A "bind" key that names no bindable field of the node. |
| `reserved_bind_path` | warning | A binding path that is kept but not applied yet. |
| `expression_syntax` | error | A "${" that is not closed, or an empty ${}. |
| `unknown_name` | error | An expression reads a name that is neither a declared variable nor a scope the runtime provides. |
| `unknown_trigger` | error | A reaction whose trigger type is unknown or missing: the reaction is dropped. |
| `unknown_trigger_key` | error | A key of a trigger that triggers do not read. |
| `unknown_action_type` | error | An action type no declaration knows: the runtime skips it. |
| `unknown_action_key` | error | A key of an action that its type does not read. |
| `unknown_target_node` | error | An action or condition names a node id that is not in the document. |
| `unknown_screen` | error | A navigate or openModal names a screen (canvas or layout id) that does not exist. |
| `unknown_variable` | error | An action or trigger names a variable that is not declared. |
| `invalid_reaction` | error | A reaction or action that is not an object, or an action list that is not a list. |
| `invalid_variable` | error | A variable without a name, with an unknown type, or whose value its type cannot hold. |
| `duplicate_variable` | error | Two variables of the same name in one scope. |
| `unknown_scope` | error | Variables or conditions keyed by an id that is not a canvas of the document (nor page_variables). |
| `invalid_condition` | error | A condition, branch, predicate or set entry of the wrong shape. |
| `unknown_breakpoint` | error | A canvas, variant or media rule names a breakpoint the project does not define. |
| `invalid_media` | error | A "media" rule of the wrong shape: no condition (minWidth, maxWidth, orientation), a width that is neither px nor a breakpoint name, a minWidth above its maxWidth, or a patch key that cannot vary by screen size. |
| `media_overridden` | warning | A media rule patches a field the node also binds: the binding wins, so the patch never shows. |
| `unknown_theme_name` | error | A color or text style names a color or text style the project's theme (the site manifest's "theme") does not have: it would show transparent or unstyled. |
| `invalid_theme` | error | The site manifest's "theme" is not of the right shape: colors are "#AARRGGBB" (or another color's name), text styles are TextStyle objects, media rules patch colors and textStyles. |
| `duplicate_breakpoint_canvas` | error | Two canvases of one screen are the design for the same breakpoint. |
| `screen_without_breakpoint` | warning | A canvas grouped into a screen (props.screen) that names no breakpoint: it shows only below the narrowest. |
| `duplicate_id` | warning | The same node id in two documents of one project: each document keeps its own, but reports and the render command's steps name nodes by id. |
| `unknown_component` | error | A call names a component type (UpperCamelCase) that no definition of the project declares: it renders as an empty box of its size. |
| `duplicate_component` | error | Two definitions declare the same component type, or a component type is also a catalog type: there is no shadowing. |
| `component_cycle` | error | A component calls itself, directly or through other components: it can never finish rendering. |
| `component_id_mismatch` | error | A component document whose file name (or "id") is not its widget type: a file holds the component it is named after. |
| `invalid_component` | error | A component document of the wrong shape: a "widget" without a type, a type that is not UpperCamelCase, or not exactly one root. |
| `missing_prop` | error | A call does not set a parameter the component declares as required. |
| `unknown_event` | error | An event reaction (or a componentEvent action) names an event the component does not declare, or sits on a node that is not a component call. |
| `call_field_not_allowed` | error | A field on a call that belongs to the definition (decoration, layout.padding): the call gives size and placement only. |
| `slot_outside_component` | warning | A slot node in a document that is not a component: nothing fills it, its own children show. |
| `root_placement_bound` | warning | A component root binds its size or placement: the call sizes and places the root, so the binding is dropped. |
| `repeated_subtree` | info | A subtree written several times over, node for node (ids and names aside): a component, or a list template, would write it once. |

The render step adds what only rendering shows: `render_exception` (naming the node), `action_error`,
`interaction_failed`, `tap_no_reaction`, `layout_overflow`, `offscreen`, `text_clipped`, `text_truncated`,
`text_no_color`, `missing_glyph`, `icon_not_drawn`, `expression_not_evaluated`, `path_overflow`, `font_fallback`,
`image_failed`, `image_network`, `empty_screen`, `invalid_json`; formulas are parsed by the SDK's own parser
there, so formula syntax errors and unknown names in formulas are reported only by the render command.

<a id="guide-pitfalls"></a>
## 18. Rules that are easy to get wrong

1. Every node needs `layout.width` and `layout.height`; without them it is 0 × 0.
2. Every text needs `style.color`; without it, it is white.
3. Padding and margin are a number or four numbers, never two.
4. Colors are `#AARRGGBB`, `#RRGGBB` or a theme color's name; declare the palette and type scale in the theme
   first and name them ([the theme](#guide-theme)).
5. Columns center their children across by default: write `"crossAxisAlignment": "start"` for left-aligned
   content.
6. A screen taller than the window needs a scrolling body column.
7. Values in `props`, `layout` and `decoration` are literal; expressions go in `bind` (except `props.text`).
8. `x`/`y` only work under a `stack`; `flex`/`align` only under a `row` or `column`.
9. Ids are map keys; a child is listed in exactly one parent; canvases are only in `roots`.
10. Per-breakpoint canvases have separate nodes: shared state lives in `page_variables`.
11. `fill` takes all the room it is given; cap it with `constraints.maxWidth`. Where its parent gives no room
    on that axis (it hugs it), a fill is its design number (`fill_fallback`).
12. A backslash inside a formula is written twice in JSON: `"${= matches(code, '^\\d{4}$')}"`.
13. `${...}` reads a name; a literal value is a formula: `${= false}`, not `${false}`.
14. A node hidden by a binding, condition or media rule takes no room or slot; `"visible": false` written on the
    node with nothing to show it keeps its room.
15. A `path` (and a box's `path`) is drawn in its box's own pixels from the top left and is not clipped to the box
    (as Flutter's `CustomPaint`): give a `path` node a `viewBox` to scale it, or clip an ancestor.
16. A `spacer` takes the free space only in a row or column with room to spare (a `fill` or fixed main size).
17. Where CSS and Flutter differ, the model follows Flutter, except where it says so: rows and columns shrink
    children that do not fit toward their content (`squeezeChildren`, default true, as CSS flex items shrink; false
    is Flutter's overflow); `basis`, `order` and `minCrossAxisExtent` are CSS's; a negative margin is not CSS's.
18. Repeated content from data: a `gridView` with `minCrossAxisExtent` for columns, a `listView` for a list; a
    wrapping `listView` runs along its `scrollDirection`.

<a id="guide-components"></a>
## 19. Sections and components

A page can be split into parts, each in a file of its own: a **component** is a document with one root (not a
canvas) and a `widget` declaration, and a page (or another component) **calls** it with one node whose `type` is
the component's type. A **section** is a component used once (a header, a hero, an FAQ band). It is Flutter's
widget class: the declaration is its constructor, a call is `PlanCard(price: 47, ...)`.

| Here | Flutter |
|---|---|
| a component document | a `StatelessWidget` / `StatefulWidget` class, in its own file |
| `widget.props` (parameters) | the constructor's named parameters, with types and defaults |
| a call `{"type": "PlanCard", "props": {...}}` | `PlanCard(...)` in a parent's `build` |
| `${props.price}` in the definition | `widget.price` |
| the definition's own `variables` (one set per instance) | the `State`'s fields |
| a `slot` node, the call's `children` / `slots` | `child`, `children`, `Widget title` parameters, placed in `build` |
| `widget.events`, `componentEvent`, the call's `event` reaction | a `ValueChanged<T>` / `VoidCallback` parameter (`onChanged`) |
| a `variable` parameter | a `ValueNotifier<T>` passed in |
| `site.json` | the app's `lib/`: its pages and its globals |

A definition (`components/Chip.json`; the file is named after the type):

```json
{"schema": 3, "id": "Chip", "roots": ["chip"],
 "widget": {"type": "Chip", "doc": "A label with a remove button.", "children": "list", "slots": ["leading"],
   "props": [
     {"key": "label", "type": {"kind": "string", "flutter": "String"}, "default": "Chip", "required": true},
     {"key": "selected", "type": {"kind": "variable", "of": {"kind": "boolean", "flutter": "bool"}}, "default": ""}],
   "events": [{"key": "onRemove", "payload": {"kind": "string", "flutter": "String"}}]},
 "variables": {"chip": [{"name": "hovered", "type": "boolean", "value": false}]},
 "previews": [{"name": "Selected", "size": [240, 48], "props": {"label": "Design", "selected": true}}],
 "nodes": {
  "chip": {"type": "row", "children": ["lead", "text", "extra", "remove"], "props": {"spacing": 6},
           "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": 36, "padding": [12, 0, 8, 0]},
           "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFE8EAF6"}], "radius": 18},
           "bind": {"decoration.fills[0].color": "${= props.selected ? '#FF3F51B5' : '#FFE8EAF6'}"},
           "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"},
                        "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "props.selected", "op": "toggle"}]}]},
  "lead": {"type": "slot", "props": {"name": "leading"}},
  "text": {"type": "text", "props": {"text": "${props.label}", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF1A237E"}},
           "layout": {"width": {"hug": 60}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
           "bind": {"props.style.color": "${= props.selected ? '#FFFFFFFF' : '#FF1A237E'}"}},
  "extra": {"type": "slot"},
  "remove": {"type": "icon", "props": {"icon": "close", "color": "#FF5C6BC0"},
             "layout": {"width": 20, "height": 20},
             "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"},
                          "actions": [{"type": "componentEvent", "event": "onRemove", "value": "${props.label}"}]}]}
 }}
```

And calls to it, in a page's `nodes` (the page declares `tag` and `removed`):

```json
"nodes": {
  "design": {"type": "Chip", "props": {"label": "Design", "selected": "tag"},
             "slots": {"leading": "dot"}, "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": 36},
             "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "event", "event": "onRemove"},
                          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "removed", "value": "${result}"}]}]},
  "dot": {"type": "box", "layout": {"width": 8, "height": 8}, "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF4CAF50"}], "radius": 4}},
  "tags": {"type": "listView", "children": ["tagChip"], "bind": {"data": "${tags}"},
           "props": {"scrollDirection": "horizontal", "spacing": 8}, "layout": {"width": {"fill": 360}, "height": 36}},
  "tagChip": {"type": "Chip", "bind": {"props.label": "${item.name}"}, "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"fill": 36}}}
}
```

**Parameters.** Declared in `widget.props` as the catalog declares any prop: `key`, `type` (`kind` and the
Flutter type; `min`, `max`, enum `values`, list `item`), `default`, `doc`, and `"required": true` for one a call
must set. The kinds: `boolean` (`bool`), `integer` (`int`), `number` (`double`), `string` (`String`),
`enumeration` (with `values`), `value` (a value type: `{"kind": "value", "flutter": "Color"}`, also `EdgeInsets`,
`Alignment`, `IconData`...), `list` (with `item`), `object` (a model: `TextStyle`, `Paint`), `json` (any data: a
record, `{"kind": "json", "flutter": "Map<String, dynamic>"}`) and `variable` (with `of`, below). Inside, read them as `${props.<key>}`. A call sets them as any node's props: a literal in `props`, an
expression in `bind` (`"props.label": "${item.name}"`). Validation checks every call against the declaration:
unknown keys, wrong types and bounds, missing required ones, children and slots the component does not take.

**What a definition reads.** Its parameters (`props`), its own variables (one set per instance: two chips are
hovered apart), the project's variables (`site.json`, below) and the runtime's scopes (`screen`, `route`,
`theme`, `auth`...); inside its own lists, `item` and `index`. **Never the caller's variables**: the same chip works
on any page. What a section needs from its page comes in as a parameter.

**`variable` parameters** share state with the caller: `{"kind": "variable", "of": {"kind": "boolean"}}`. The
call passes the *name* of one of its variables (`"selected": "tag"`); inside, `${props.selected}` reads it live and
`setVariable "props.selected"` writes it. A header and a menu both taking `"menuOpen": "menuOpen"` open and close
the page's one menu.

**Slots.** A `slot` node in the definition is replaced by what the call passes: the call's `children` for the
slot named `children` (the default name; declare `"children": "list"`), or the call's `slots[name]` for a named
slot (declare it in `widget.slots`). With nothing passed, the slot shows its own children. What is passed belongs
to the caller: it is stored in the page and reads the page's variables.

**Events.** Declared in `widget.events`; fired inside with `{"type": "componentEvent", "event": "onRemove",
"value": ...}`; handled by the call's reaction `{"trigger": {"type": "event", "event": "onRemove"}}`, which runs in
the caller's scope with the value as `${result}`. An event nobody handles does nothing.

**Size and place.** The call and the definition's root are one box: the call's `layout` sizes and places it
(width, height, flex, margin, x/y, align, constraints); the root keeps its padding, decoration and contents. A call
has no `decoration` and no `layout.padding`. The root's own size is the design size its previews and new calls
use. `visible` hides the instance when either the call or the root is hidden.

**Ids are local.** A definition's ids are its own (`text`, `remove`); a page may use the same ids, and
diagnostics name a node of an instance by its path, so the two never mix. An action inside a definition that names
a node (`scrollTo`, `animate`, `focus`) acts on that node of its own instance: two cards each scroll their own
list. Tools name a
node inside an instance by its **path**: the call ids from the page down, then the node's id
(`design/remove`, `plans/card1/cta`); `#n` picks the n-th copy a list repeats (`tagChip#2/text`).

**A site.** A directory with a `site.json` is a site: its pages, its components and its project variables, read by
bare name in every page and component (a page or component variable of the same name is `duplicate_variable`).

```json
{"schema": 3, "pages": ["pages/home.json"], "components": ["components/Chip.json"],
 "variables": [{"name": "tags", "type": "list", "value": [{"name": "Design"}, {"name": "Code"}]}]}
```

Without `components`, the files under `components/` are the site's components.

**Rendering one part.** `tool/render/render.sh site --out out --component Chip` renders the component alone, once
per preview at its size; `--props '{"label": "Long label"}'` renders one parameter set at each size, and
`--slots fixture.json` (`{"children": [ids], "slots": {"leading": id}, "nodes": {...}}`) passes slot content.
Steps take paths: `--tap design/remove`.

`--components-all` renders every component of the site that way in one run (`<Type>-<preview>@<w>x<h>.png`):
the quickest look at every part a page can call.

**Per instance.** Everything a definition keeps is kept per instance, as a Flutter `State` is: its variables, its
interaction states, the values a `setValue` (or `setVariant`) sets on its nodes (set inside an instance, they change
that instance's node only). A variable with `"persist": true` is kept per instance path
(`codelessly.component.<Type>.<path>.<name>` in the app's storage). When an instance leaves the screen (a list
item scrolled away, data that shrank), what it kept goes with it, as a `State` is disposed; shown again, it starts
afresh (a persisted variable from its stored value).

**A slot inside a list of the definition** shows what the call passes once per item, as a Flutter `child` placed
in each item an `itemBuilder` builds: the same nodes, built in the caller's scope. They read the caller's
variables, not the item: to show the item, make it a parameter of a component the list calls. Tools name each copy
by the caller's path with `#n` (`note#2`).

**Published.** A published site carries its components beside its pages (each at
`publish/{project}/components/{Type}`, with a version and a digest; a bundle holds them in its `components` map),
and an app loads the ones a screen calls with the screen, caches them, and follows a republished one: every
instance updates where it is, without reloading the pages that call it. Nothing to write in the app: a
`CodelesslyWidget` showing a published site with components just works. A call whose component can't be loaded
is an empty box of its size until it arrives (`component_missing` in the app's error log).

**A hint.** Validation reports `repeated_subtree` (an INFO, not a problem) when a document writes the same subtree
of three or more nodes several times over, node for node but for ids and names: that subtree is a component (or a
list template) waiting to be made.

**When to make what.**

* **List template**: one shape repeated from data in one parent. When the item is more than about five nodes, or
  appears elsewhere too, make the template one call node (`"bind": {"props.plan": "${item}"}`).
* **Component**: the same structure in two or more places with different values (buttons, cards, chips, rows),
  or a part others will reuse. Data comes in as parameters. Four near-identical columns of a table, or three plan
  cards, are one component (or one list template) called four or three times, not four copies.
* **Section**: a top-level band of a page (header, hero, plans, FAQ, footer), in its own file when it is more
  than about 15 nodes or someone will edit it alone, even if it is used once. Parameters only for what it shares
  with its page (`variable` parameters for state both change).

**Validation codes** for components: `unknown_component` (a call to a type no definition declares),
`duplicate_component`, `component_cycle` (a component calling itself, directly or through others),
`component_id_mismatch` (the file is not named after its type), `invalid_component`, `missing_prop`,
`unknown_event`, `call_field_not_allowed`, `slot_outside_component`, `root_placement_bound`. The render command
adds `component_missing` (a call rendered without its definition: an empty box of its size).

Components made by copying a node tree into the library (`ComponentLink`, DESIGN.md §4.2) are still read and
drawn as before: their instances are copies.

<a id="guide-edit"></a>
## 20. Editing with ops, and streaming

A document is built and changed with six **edit operations**, each addressed by node id: what an agent sends in a
`ui_apply` tool call, what `codelessly apply` takes, and what an app's `UiSession` applies while a model streams
(`applyOps`, `decodeOps`, `OpStreamDecoder` in `package:codelessly_api/core.dart`). Generation is just the first
batch of ops; every change after it is a few more.

| Op | Fields | Means | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set` | `id`, `node`, `nodes`, `parent`, `index`, `slot`, `placeholders` | Create node `id` (or replace it: the result says which), optionally placed under `parent` at `index` (default: last) or in `slot`. `node` is the node as the document holds it under "nodes": its `children` may list ids that arrive in later ops (pending until then). `nodes` sets several nodes at once (id → node), in order. `placeholders` gives a size (a layout fragment) to show for a pending child until it arrives. | `{"op":"set","id":"faqTitle","parent":"faqSec","index":0,"node":{"type":"text","layout":{"width":{"hug":120},"height":{"hug":28}},"props":{"text":"Questions","style":{"fontSize":22,"fontWeight":700,"color":"#FF111827"}}}}` |
| `patch` | `id` (required), `patch` (required) | Merge `patch` into node `id` (RFC 7396): objects merge, arrays and scalars replace, null deletes a key. Shaped like the node (`{"props": {"text": "Book a demo"}}`). It cannot change `children`, `slots` or `type`. | `{"op":"patch","id":"heroTitle","patch":{"props":{"text":"Book a demo","style":{"color":"#FF0F766E"}}}}` |
| `move` | `id` (required), `parent` (required), `index`, `slot` | Move node `id` (with its subtree) under `parent` at `index` (default: last), or into `slot`. Reorder: move within the same parent. | `{"op":"move","id":"faqSec","parent":"page","index":2}` |
| `remove` | `ids` (required) | Remove the nodes `ids` and everything under them; their parents stop listing them. | `{"op":"remove","ids":["promoBanner"]}` |
| `vars` | `scope` (required), `set`, `remove` | Variables of `scope` (a canvas id, or "page_variables"): `set` maps a name to its new value, or to a full variable object (`{"type": "boolean", "value": false}`) to declare it; `remove` lists names to remove. Bindings that read them update at once. | `{"op":"vars","scope":"pricing","set":{"annual":true}}` |
| `roots` | `roots` (required) | Set the document's canvases, in order. A root may name a canvas that arrives in a later op. | `{"op":"roots","roots":["home"]}` |

Rules:

* A `patch` is an RFC 7396 merge patch on one node, shaped like the node: objects merge, lists and values replace,
  `null` deletes a key. It never changes `children`, `slots` or `type` (`structural_key_in_patch`): child lists
  change only through `set` (with `parent`), `move` and `remove`.
* A `set` of an id that exists replaces the node (the result says which ids it created). Replacing a node that had
  children it no longer lists is `would_orphan`: keep them, move or remove them first, or patch instead.
* Each op is checked on its own, against what it touched: its structure (one parent, no cycle, no canvas as a child,
  a parent that takes children there), the trust profile, and the nodes' fields (the strict validator of
  §17 on the nodes the op created or changed, their parents and children). A rejected op changes nothing; the others
  apply (with `"atomic": true`, all or none).
* A batch may carry `"baseRev"`, the revision the author read: a patch of a field, or a set of a node, that another
  author changed since is `stale_rev`, with the current value. Every applied batch has inverse ops: applied
  atomically, they restore the document (undo).

The ops that build the smallest document of §1, top-down, as a model streams them:

```json
{
  "ops": [
    {"op": "roots", "roots": ["home"]},
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "home",
      "node": {
        "type": "canvas",
        "name": "Home",
        "slots": {"body": "page"},
        "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
        "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "page",
      "node": {
        "type": "column",
        "children": ["title", "body"],
        "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
        "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 12}
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "title",
      "node": {
        "type": "text",
        "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 34}},
        "props": {"text": "Hello", "style": {"fontWeight": 700, "fontSize": 28, "color": "#FF111827"}}
      }
    },
    {
      "op": "set",
      "id": "body",
      "node": {
        "type": "text",
        "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
        "props": {
          "text": "A column with two texts, filling the screen's width.",
          "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FF4B5563", "height": 1.4}
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Then a follow-up instruction ("add a button under the title, drop the body text, make the title say Welcome") is
a few ops, not a new document:

```json
{"ops": [
  {"op": "set", "id": "cta", "parent": "page", "index": 1,
   "node": {"type": "row", "children": ["ctaText"], "layout": {"width": {"hug": 140}, "height": 44, "padding": [16, 0, 16, 0]},
            "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 10}}},
  {"op": "set", "id": "ctaText", "node": {"type": "text", "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
            "props": {"text": "Get started", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}}}},
  {"op": "remove", "ids": ["body"]},
  {"op": "patch", "id": "title", "patch": {"props": {"text": "Welcome"}}},
  {"op": "vars", "scope": "home", "set": {"taps": {"type": "integer", "value": 0}}},
  {"op": "patch", "id": "cta", "patch": {"actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"},
            "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "taps", "op": "add", "value": 1}]}]}},
  {"op": "move", "id": "cta", "parent": "page", "index": 0}
]}
```

A batch with a mistake: the second op misspells `fills`. It is rejected with a code, the path and a suggestion; the
first applies:

```json
{
  "ops": [
    {"op": "patch", "id": "title", "patch": {"props": {"text": "Welcome back"}}},
    {"op": "patch", "id": "title", "patch": {"decoration": {"fill": [{"color": "#FFF1F5F9"}]}}}
  ]
}
```

The result (`EditResult.toModelJson()`, the tool result):

```json
{
  "rev": 1,
  "applied": [0],
  "rejected": [
    {
      "op": 1,
      "code": "unknown_decoration_key",
      "path": "/nodes/title/decoration/fill",
      "message": "decoration has no \"fill\".",
      "nodeId": "title",
      "expected": [
        "fills",
        "strokes",
        "strokeWidth",
        "strokeAlign",
        "strokeSides",
        "strokeCap",
        "dashPattern",
        "radius",
        "effects",
        "clip",
        "blendMode",
        "foregroundFills",
        "shape"
      ],
      "suggestion": "fills"
    }
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

### Streaming

LLM APIs deliver a tool call's input as text deltas cut anywhere. `OpStreamDecoder` yields each op the moment its
closing brace arrives (inside a `set` with `nodes`, each node as its own brace closes), whatever the cuts; a stream
cut mid-op keeps every complete op and reports the tail (`truncated_op`). While a document streams in, it is
incomplete by nature:

* **Order.** Root first, then top-down: the `roots` op, the canvas, its container, then each section complete before
  the next. Nothing breaks if a model does otherwise.
* **Forward references.** A child id listed before its node arrives is **pending**, not an error; a reference to a
  node, screen or variable that has not arrived yet (a state that patches it, a navigation to it) is a warning while
  the stream runs (`applyOps(..., incomplete: true)`). When the stream ends, `endOfStream` reports every id still
  dangling (`dangling_child`), so the model can send it.
* **Rendering** (the SDK's `UiSession`): nothing paints until a root canvas has content; a pending child takes no
  room (or the size a `set`'s `placeholders` gave it); a container none of whose children has arrived waits for
  its first, so no empty shells flash; text and values are never shown half-written (an op applies only whole).

### What a model reads

`outline(document)` is one row per node, `[id, type, label, depth, {what is bound, states, triggers}]`, a sixth to
a seventh of the document's size (the two m05 pages: 6.7 KB for 147 nodes against 47.6 KB, 8.3 KB for 196 nodes
against 55.4 KB). `readUi` answers the `ui_read` tool: the outline, or whole nodes by id.

The two tools (`uiTools(catalog)`), their input schemas generated from the op declarations and the catalog's
node types (the agent profile over the core: [ui_tools.json](ui_tools.json)):

```json
[
  {
    "name": "ui_apply",
    "description": "Build or change the UI. The UI is one document: a flat map of nodes by id, each a Flutter-like widget (type, layout, decoration, props, children). Ops apply in order: set (create or replace a node, optionally placing it under a parent), patch (RFC 7396 merge patch on one node; null deletes a key), move, remove, vars (set or declare variables) and roots (the screens). Ids are the addresses: choose short readable ids. A node may list children that arrive in later ops. When building, write top-down: the roots op and the canvas first, then each container before its children, section by section, so the UI paints as it streams. To change an existing UI, send only the small ops the change needs (patch a prop instead of re-sending a node). The result lists the ops that were rejected with a code, a path and a suggestion: fix and resend only those.",
    "input_schema": "(see ui_tools.json)"
  },
  {
    "name": "ui_read",
    "description": "Read the current UI before changing it: the outline (one row per node: id, type, label, depth, what is bound), or full nodes by id. Read the outline first; ask for full nodes only for the ones you will change.",
    "input_schema": "(see ui_tools.json)"
  }
]
```

### The trust profile

`TrustProfile` is what an edited document may use: node types and action types (a restricted catalog,
`profile.restrict(catalog)`), scripts, link and image hosts, navigation, and limits (nodes, depth, text length, ops
per call). `TrustProfile.agent`, the default for agent-written UI, allows the core's node types and its local
actions (variables, values, in-document navigation, modals, toasts, scrolling, animation, `componentEvent`): no
scripts, no links, no host functions, no feature library's types. A violation is `capability_not_allowed` or
`limit_exceeded`, with the op and the path.

`componentEvent` in a document that is not a component (an agent's UI) is the event to the document's host: the
session delivers it to the app, which sends it to the model.

### Codes of the edit layer

| Code | Rejects the op | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_op` | yes | An op that is not an object, or names no known "op" (set, patch, move, remove, vars, roots). |
| `missing_field` | yes | An op without a field it needs ("id", "node", "patch", "parent", "ids", "scope", "roots"). |
| `wrong_type` | yes | A field of an op with the wrong JSON type (an id that is not text, a node that is not an object). |
| `unknown_id` | yes | A patch, move or remove of a node the document does not have, or a set or move under a parent it does not have. |
| `structural_key_in_patch` | yes | A patch that changes "children" or "slots" (or "type"): child lists change only through set, move and remove; a type through set. |
| `stale_rev` | yes | The op changes a field another author changed after the batch's "baseRev": re-read the node (ui_read) and decide. |
| `would_orphan` | yes | A set that replaces a node and drops children it had: they would be left under no parent. Keep them in "children", move or remove them first, or use patch. |
| `multiple_parents` | yes | The op would list a node under a second parent (or twice in one): a node has one parent. Use move to change its parent. |
| `cycle` | yes | The op would put a node inside its own subtree. |
| `canvas_as_child` | yes | The op would place a canvas under a parent: canvases are only roots. |
| `invalid_parent` | yes | A set or move under a parent that takes no children there: a type without children, or a slot the type does not have. |
| `dangling_child` | yes | At the end of the stream, a child or slot id that names no node (it was pending and never arrived). |
| `unreachable_node` | no (a warning) | At the end of the stream, a node no root reaches (nothing lists it as a child or slot). |
| `pending_child` | no (a warning) | A child or slot id the op lists that has not arrived yet: accepted while streaming, an error (dangling_child) if it never comes. |
| `capability_not_allowed` | yes | The op uses a node type, action, script, link, image host or navigation target the session's trust profile does not allow. |
| `limit_exceeded` | yes | The op would exceed a limit of the trust profile (nodes, depth, text length, ops per call). |
| `truncated_op` | yes | The stream ended inside an op: what arrived of it was not applied. |
| `invalid_json` | yes | The tool input is not JSON where an op was expected. |
| `invalid_variable` | yes | A vars op that declares a variable without a name, or sets one with a value its type cannot hold. |
| `unknown_variable` | no (a warning) | A vars op that sets (or removes) a variable the scope does not declare: declare it with a full variable object. |

<a id="page-layout"></a>
# Layout

A node's `"layout"` object: its size, spacing, and placement in its parent. See the guide's
[Layout](#guide-layout) section for how the modes behave, with examples.

`width` and `height` are an [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize): a number (fixed) or `{"fill" | "hug" |
"flexible" | "fixed": number}`. `x` and `y` are an [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition). The default
size is fixed 0: a node without a width and a height draws nothing.

## Fields

<a id="layout-width"></a>
<a id="layout-height"></a>
<a id="layout-constraints"></a>
<a id="layout-margin"></a>
<a id="layout-padding"></a>
<a id="layout-rotation"></a>
<a id="layout-aspectRatio"></a>
<a id="layout-flex"></a>
<a id="layout-squeezable"></a>
<a id="layout-x"></a>
<a id="layout-y"></a>
<a id="layout-align"></a>
<a id="layout-order"></a>
<a id="layout-basis"></a>
- `width`: [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize) = `0`
- `height`: [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize) = `0`
- `constraints`: [BoxConstraints](#type-BoxConstraints) = `{}`
- `margin`: [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) = `0`
- `padding`: [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) = `0`
- `rotation`: double = `0`
- `aspectRatio`: double = unset (≥ 0)
- `flex`: int = `1` (≥ 0)
- `squeezable`: bool = `false`
- `x`: [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition) = `{"start":0}`
- `y`: [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition) = `{"start":0}`
- `align`: [Alignment](#type-Alignment) = unset
- `order`: int = `0`
- `basis`: double = unset (≥ 0)

Read by decoding but not declared as fields: `widthFactor`, `heightFactor`. A share (0–1 and up) of the room its parent gives it on that axis (`FractionallySizedBox`): a progress bar's fill is `widthFactor: 0.6` of its track. Null: sized by `width` / `height`. Bindable (`layout.widthFactor`).

## Which sizing modes each parent allows

| Parent | Width may be | Height may be |
|---|---|---|
| `row` | fixed, fill, flexible, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, flexible, hug |
| `row` with {"wrap":true} | fixed, fill (with `basis`), hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` with {"scrollable":true} | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, hug |
| `row` with {"scrollable":true,"scrollDirection":"horizontal"} | fixed, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `stack` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `canvas` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `listView` | fill | fixed, hug |
| `listView` with {"itemExtent":80} | fill | fill |
| `gridView` | fill | fill |
| `pageView` | fill | fill |

Why a mode is not allowed, as the declarations say it:

- Flexible only applies in a row or column, along its main axis.
- A wrapping row lays its children out in runs: they keep their own size along it, unless they set layout.basis (CSS flex-basis): then a filling child grows to share its line.
- The column scrolls: its content has no end to fill to.
- The row scrolls: its content has no end to fill to.
- Items in a list always fill across it.
- A list is unbounded along its scroll axis: items cannot fill it. Set an item extent.
- The list gives every item its item extent: they fill it.
- Grid cells size their children: they fill them.
- Pages size their children: they fill them.

<a id="page-decoration"></a>
# Decoration

A node's `"decoration"` object: what its box paints. Types without a box decoration (see
[node types](#page-nodes)) keep only blur effects. Fills paint bottom to top under the node's content;
`foregroundFills` paint over it, **children included** (Flutter's `foregroundDecoration`): a scrim in a photo's
`foregroundFills` darkens a caption inside the photo node too; put the caption after a gradient box instead.
Every color may be a theme color's name (`"ember"`).

## Fields

- `fills`: List<[Paint](#type-Paint)> = `[]`
- `strokes`: List<[Paint](#type-Paint)> = `[]`
- `strokeWidth`: double = `1` (≥ 0)
- `strokeAlign`: [StrokeAlign](#enum-StrokeAlign) = `"inside"` (`inside`, `center`, `outside`)
- `strokeSides`: [StrokeSides](#enum-StrokeSides) = `"all"`

<a id="page-values"></a>
# Value types, models and enums

How values are written in JSON. **Value types** are written in a compact form of their own (a color as
`"#AARRGGBB"`). **Models** are JSON objects with the fields listed. **Enums** are written as the value's name.
Decoding is lenient and never fails: a value it cannot read becomes the field's default, which is why
validation reports it.

## Value types

<a id="type-Alignment"></a>
### Alignment

JSON: [x, y] from -1 to 1, or a name: topLeft, topCenter, topRight, centerLeft, center, centerRight, bottomLeft, bottomCenter, bottomRight.

<a id="type-AxisPosition"></a>
### AxisPosition

JSON: a number (distance from the start) or {"start": d}, {"end": d}, {"start": a, "end": b}, {"align": -1..1}, {"relative": d}.

<a id="type-AxisSize"></a>
### AxisSize

JSON: a number (fixed) or {"fill"|"flexible"|"hug"|"fixed": number}.

<a id="type-BorderRadius"></a>
### BorderRadius

JSON: a number (every corner), [x, y] (every corner elliptical) or [topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft] (each a number or [x, y]).

<a id="type-BoxConstraints"></a>
### BoxConstraints

JSON: {"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"} (each optional, numbers >= 0).

<a id="type-Color"></a>
### Color

JSON: "#AARRGGBB" or "#RRGGBB" (hex, alpha first).

<a id="type-EdgeInsets"></a>
### EdgeInsets

JSON: a number (all sides) or [left, top, right, bottom].

<a id="type-FontFeature"></a>
### FontFeature

JSON: an OpenType tag ("tnum", "ss01") or "tag=value" ("liga=0").

<a id="type-FontWeight"></a>
### FontWeight

JSON: 100, 200 ... 900.

<a id="type-IconData"></a>
### IconData

JSON: a Material icon name ("check_circle", "lock_open_rounded"), an image URL, or {"type": "MATERIAL_ICON", "name", "style"}.

<a id="type-Offset"></a>
### Offset

JSON: [dx, dy].

<a id="type-Rect"></a>
### Rect

JSON: [left, top, width, height].

<a id="type-Size"></a>
### Size

JSON: [width, height].

## Models

Objects with declared fields. Keys not listed are reported by validation (`unknown_field`).

<a id="page-behaviors"></a>
# Behaviors

Behaviors are what a node does beyond its layout and paint: motion, interaction states, tooltips, drag and drop,
scroll effects. Each is a key written directly on the node (not under `props`), sparse: leave it out for none. The
guide's [states](#guide-states) section shows `states`, the most used one.

<a id="page-triggers"></a>
# Triggers

A reaction (`"actions": [{"trigger": {...}, "actions": [...]}]` on a node) starts on its trigger. In the chain,
`${result}` first holds the trigger's event (where a click landed, an input's new value). Screen triggers (`load`,
`valueChanged`, `timer`, `keyDown`...) are set on the canvas.

<a id="page-actions"></a>
# Actions

An action is a JSON object `{"type": "<type>", ...fields}`, run in order in a reaction's chain. Text fields are
expressions (`"${count}"`, `"${= a + 1}"`). A field holding nested actions (`then`, `else`, `onSuccess`...) is a
list of actions. A key not listed for the type is dropped by decoding and reported by validation
(`unknown_action_key`).

## Fields every action has

- `enabled`: bool = `true`
- `nonBlocking`: bool = `false`
- `when`: Object = unset

Fields holding nested action chains (a list of actions): `then`, `else`, `actions`, `onSuccess`, `onError`, `cancelActions`.

<a id="page-bindings"></a>
# Bindings and expressions

`"bind"` on a node maps a **binding path** (a path into the node's JSON) to an expression; the field at the path
takes the expression's value. Paths: `visible`, `opacity`, `layout.<field>`, `decoration.<field>` (with
`[index]`, a paint's `id` or `*` into lists), `props.<prop>` and deeper fields of model props, `data`, `selected`,
`disabled`, and the behavior keys. Values are read loosely: `"12"` is a number, `1` and `"true"` are true,
`"#FF0000"` is a color; a value that cannot be read leaves the field as it was.

Expressions: `${path}` reads a value (`user.name`, `items[0].price`, `pal[item.kind]`), `${= formula}` computes
one ([formula functions](#page-formulas)). A binding that is exactly one expression keeps the value's type.

A text's `props.text` may hold expressions directly. A literal `$` right before one is text: `"$${price}"` shows
`$47`. There is no escape for a literal `${`.

A media rule's patch may bind too (`"patch": {"bind": {"visible": "${= !open}"}}`): the binding holds at the
rule's sizes only, and `null` drops one of the node's own there.

## Named paths

| Path | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `visible` |  |
| `opacity` |  |
| `selected` | Interaction states driven by data: true puts the node in `WidgetState.selected` / `WidgetState.disabled`, so its state styles (`states.selected`, `states.disabled`) patch it and its descendants, as hover and press do (`"selected": "${= item.id == selectedId}"`). |
| `disabled` |  |
| `data` | The items a repeating widget (list, grid, page view) builds one per. |
| `layout.width` |  |
| `layout.height` |  |
| `layout.flex` |  |
| `layout.rotation` |  |
| `layout.margin` |  |
| `layout.padding` |  |
| `layout.x` |  |
| `layout.y` |  |
| `decoration.radius` |  |
| `decoration.strokeWidth` |  |
| `scale` |  |
| `textDirection` |  |

## What each path expects

A formula gives the value as the field is written in JSON: a number, `true`/`false`, a name for an enum, a list or an object for the fields written that way. A value of another shape is not read and the field keeps its value.

| Path | Type | A formula gives |
|---|---|---|
| `visible` | `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `opacity` | `double` | a number |
| `selected` | `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `disabled` | `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `data` | `List` | a list |

| `layout.height` | `AxisSize` | a number (fixed) or {"fill"\|"flexible"\|"hug"\|"fixed": number} |
